Define an instrument for synthetic respondents

Source: R/instrument.R
sc_instrument.Rd

sc_instrument() describes the survey that synthetic respondents take: The items, the response scale and the instructions. generate_synthetic() turns it into a prompt, and the item table works as items in authenticity_benchmark().

Usage

sc_instrument(
  items,
  scale = c(1, 5),
  labels = NULL,
  instructions = sc_default_instructions,
  name = "Instrument"
)

Arguments

items

a data frame with an item column (short names such as "H1") and a statement column (the item text), plus optional scale (or trait), facet and reverse columns, as in hexaco_items. A character vector of statements also works; the items are then named i1, i2, and so on.

scale

the lowest and highest response categories, for example c(1, 5).

labels

optional labels for the categories, one per category from lowest to highest. NULL uses agree-disagree labels for 5- and 7-point scales and labels the endpoints only otherwise.

instructions

the instructions shown before the items.

name

a short name for the instrument.

Value

An object of class sc_instrument.

See also

sc_personas(), generate_synthetic()

Examples

hexaco <- sc_instrument(hexaco_items, scale = c(1, 7), name = "IPIP-HEXACO")
hexaco
#> Instrument "IPIP-HEXACO": 240 items, answers 1 to 7.
#> Scales: H, E, X, A, C, O 
#>   HSinc1: I don't pretend to be more than I am.
#>   HSinc2: I use flattery to get ahead.
#>   HSinc3: I tell other people what they want to hear so that they will do what I want them to do.
#>   ... and 237 more

short <- sc_instrument(c("I am the life of the party.", "I sympathize with others."),
                       scale = c(1, 5))
short$items
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   item  statement                  
#>   <chr> <chr>                      
#> 1 i1    I am the life of the party.
#> 2 i2    I sympathize with others.
